NIRA3A.excerpt:
Sec . 3. (a) Upon the application to the President by one or more 
trade or industrial associations or groups, the President may approve 
a code or codes of fair competition for the trade or industry or sub-
division thereof, represented by the applicant or applicants, if the 
President finds (1) that such associations or groups impose no 
inequitable restrictions on admission to membership therein and are 
truly representative of such trades or industries or subdivisions 
thereof, and (2) that such code or codes are not designed to pro-
mote monopolies or to eliminate or oppress small enterprises and will 
not operate to discriminate against them, and will tend to effectuate 
the policy of this title: Provided, That such code or codes shall not 
permit monopolies or monopolistic practices: Provided further, 
That where such code or codes affect the services and welfare of 
persons engaged in other steps of the economic process, nothing in 
this section shall deprive such persons of the right to be heard prior 
to approval by the President of such code or codes. The President 
may, as a condition of his approval of any such code, impose such 
conditions (including requirements for the making of reports and 
the keeping of accounts) for the protection of consumers, competi-
tors, employees, and others, and in furtherance of the public inter-
est, and may provide such exceptions to and exemptions from the 
provisions of such code, as the President in his discretion deems 
necessary to effectuate the policy herein declared.

NIRA10.excerpt:
Sec . 10. (a) The President is authorized to prescribe such rules 
and regulations as may be necessary to carry out the purposes of 
this title, and fees for licenses and for filing codes of fair competi-
tion and agreements, and any violation of any such rule or regula-
tion shall be punishable by fine of not to exceed $500, or imprison-
ment for not to exceed six months, or both.
(b) The President may from time to time cancel or modify any 
order, approval, license, rule, or regulation issued under this title; 
and each agreement, code of fair competition, or license approved, 
prescribed, or issued under this title shall contain an express pro-
vision to that effect.

SJRES12.excerpt:
[CHAPTER 246.] JOINT RESOLUTION
To extend until April 1, 1936, certain provisions of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, and for other purposes.
Resolved by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United 
States of America in Congress assembled, That section 2 (c) of Title I 
of the National Industrial Recovery Act is amended by striking out 
“ at the expiration of two years after the date of enactment of this 
Act ” and inserting in lieu thereof “ on April 1, 1936 ”.
Sec . 2. All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power 
to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and 
providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed: 
Provided, That the exemption provided in section 5 of such title 
shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder (1) putting 
into effect the requirements of section 7 (a), including minimum 
wages, maximum hours, and prohibition of child labor; and (2) pro-
hibiting unfair competitive practices which offend against existing 
law, including the antitrust laws, or which constitute unfair methods 
of competition under the Federal Trade Commission Act, as 
amended.
Approved, June 14, 1935.

SCHECHTERDELEGATION.excerpt:
To summarize and conclude upon this point: Section 3 
of the Recovery Act is without precedent. It supplies no 
standards for any trade, industry or activity. It does not 
undertake to prescribe rules of conduct to be applied to 
particular states of fact determined by appropriate admin-
istrative procedure. Instead of prescribing rules of con-
duct, it authorizes the making of codes to prescribe them. 
For that legislative undertaking, § 3 sets up no standards, 
aside from the statement of the general aims of rehabili-
tation, correction and expansion described in section one.

propositions.proposition: An approval condition may be code-dependent, including a reporting requirement: NIRA section 3(a) expressly includes reports and accounts among approval conditions. Its grammatical placement and code-related subject matter are evidence of that relationship, but do not alone establish that all distinct future acts are extinguished by repeal.
exclusions_and_counterexamples: Do not classify every report as independent merely because it is a report. Conversely, do not classify every study/appointment as extinguished merely because it is inside a code approval.
The separate administrative/research powers and post-repeal orders are counterevidence to a universal subject-matter rule.
individual_evidence_required: For each clause identify addressee, required act, authority, relationship to the code, and whether its prospective operation requires code approval/enforcement authority.
propositions.status: research-only; not a lifecycle claim or adopted rule

propositions.proposition: June 14, 1935 is a supported statutory outer limit for prospective section-3 code approval/prescription/enforcement operation, not proof of the first ending of each command. Title I was selectively extended rather than wholly repealed.
exclusions_and_counterexamples: Schechter on May 27, 1935 must be evaluated as a potential earlier legal endpoint; this worker adopts neither the original shared analysis claim that cancellation is necessary nor a universal May 27 endpoint.
Earlier performance, own terms, supersession and cancellation can precede repeal.
individual_evidence_required: Command-specific first-ending inquiry, including effect of Schechter on the particular command and any operative earlier act.
propositions.status: research-only; not a lifecycle claim or adopted rule

propositions.proposition: Post-repeal research and administrative work was legally contemplated: EO7075 orders analysis/reporting on former codes and transfers eligible Board powers; EO7076 extends consistent existing Title I orders and agencies until April 1, 1936, excluding code approval/prescription/enforcement.
exclusions_and_counterexamples: These texts defeat a universal claim that studying a code necessarily ended June 14, but do not prove continuity of any named earlier committee, report, or unperformed appointment.
EO7252 transfers specified functions/agencies; NRA abolition alone is not proof that every earlier duty ended Jan1 1936.
individual_evidence_required: Identify whether the actual auxiliary command was still existing, legally consistent with the amended Act, transferred/continued, cancelled, or performed; no automatic Apr1 endpoint.
propositions.status: research-only; not a lifecycle claim or adopted rule

propositions.proposition: EO6686 item 6 directs an actual future study submission by the Code Authority, despite appearing among numbered findings. Its three-month term is a due date tied to an effective date, not evidence the study was made or that the command ended.
exclusions_and_counterexamples: The purpose of revising code wages/hours supports code dependence but does not itself demonstrate cancellation of the study obligation.
Approval and study submission require separate treatment.
individual_evidence_required: Held code effective date for due-date calculation; actual study/report submission or receipt; later cancellation/transfer or reasoned authority analysis; earlier-ending search.
propositions.status: research-only; not a lifecycle claim or adopted rule

propositions.proposition: EO6729 has distinct designation/cooperation/recommendation and industry-report duties. Ninety days and December 1, 1934 are deadlines; neither establishes performance. Code-inclusion purposes may limit prospective recommendations but do not prove the committee was created, dissolved, or its report submitted.
exclusions_and_counterexamples: Do not infer extinction from an expired deadline or infer nonperformance from a missing report.
Do not conflate designation of a committee with completion of its investigative/recommendation work.
individual_evidence_required: Industry designation, Administrator approval of membership, standards recommendations, industry report/receipt, and any amendment or cancellation, individually tied to the relevant duty.
propositions.status: research-only; not a lifecycle claim or adopted rule

propositions.proposition: EO6601 is a close comparator to EO6686/6729: its report direction is expressly a condition of approval, concerns code effects and possible revision, and uses a relative deadline. No source-based general distinction found here justifies closing the latter reports by repeal while keeping this one open.
exclusions_and_counterexamples: This consistency finding does not prove all three survive or all three end together. Different evidence of performance, cancellation, authority or earlier effect may distinguish them.
individual_evidence_required: Apply the same clause-level evidentiary questions; secure effective date and actual Administrator report or superseding/cancelling instrument.
propositions.status: research-only; not a lifecycle claim or adopted rule

exclusions_and_counterexamples: The formal amendment can be distinguished from future appointments and continuing study functions; a change in text does not prove those acts happened.
Do not use the Code Authority nominations as evidence the Board actually appointed members.
The APP slug says 6870 while the project candidate is 6870A; registry identity/custody needs confirmation.

propositions.proposition: EO6271 and EO6292 creation directions also carry a planning/fair-practice role to cooperate with the Administrator. Their texts do not state an end date. Similarity to EO6870A makes blanket repeal closure of one but not others insufficiently explained.
exclusions_and_counterexamples: Neither the noun committee nor Code Authority conclusively supplies legal authority or lifespan.
Code enforcement functions may end while a performed appointment, records, or a distinct research duty presents a different question.
individual_evidence_required: Constitution/member approval, identity of later body, allocated functions and subsequent instruments; separate one-time constitution from continuing activity.
propositions.status: research-only; not a lifecycle claim or adopted rule

propositions.proposition: EO6871 supplies affirmative evidence that EO6861 committee appointment, hearings, investigation and report actually occurred; the report is dated October 10, 1934. It expressly revokes only EO6861 paragraph 1 and separately continues the committee for further work.
exclusions_and_counterexamples: Performance is established for the stated earlier mission, not dissolution of the committee or formal revocation of all of EO6861.
Recital supports appointment by the report date; it does not give the exact appointment date.

individual_evidence_required: If claiming performance exhaustion, distinguish each act and its proven date/interval: appointment no later than Oct10; report Oct10; presidential possession/consideration no later than Oct12 (inference). propositions.status: research-only; not a lifecycle claim or adopted rule

propositions.proposition: EO6871 contains separable endpoints and unresolved commands: paragraph1 express revocation on issuance; paragraph2 a stay through December1; paragraphs3-5 continuation/appointment/investigation/report commands with deadlines. exclusions_and_counterexamples: The January15 report is not shown submitted merely because due. Prison Labor Compact study reaches beyond the particular code-amendment suspension; it must not be collapsed into that stay.
Own-terms stay remains subject to intervening modification; stated-date calculation is not exhaustive first-ending research.
individual_evidence_required: Separate November15 continuation report, prison-competition committee constitution and Dec1 report, Jan15 Board report, later modifications/cancellations, and authority/transfer analysis.
propositions.status: research-only; not a lifecycle claim or adopted rule

propositions.proposition: EO6513B and EO6653 stays directly suspend application of code provisions pending an Administrator determination/order. Their code-dependent prospective function cannot outlive effective operation of the suspended code, but no held later determination found in this bounded search establishes their first end.
exclusions_and_counterexamples: No later record found is not proof no determination occurred.
A condition defining the stay does not necessarily impose an independent duty to issue a determination; read the actual words.

The wording does not support a simple statement that paragraph5 requires the report within ninety days.

No assertion is made that the dependent trigger occurred or that the report obligation never arose.
